user.release_notes:
This alpha adds a standalone desktop app for Linux, macOS, and Windows alongside the Decky plugin and command-line updater.

- Browse connected devices and available firmware through a shared interface, with component illustrations and clearer controller/receiver identification.
- Install native desktop packages or standalone binaries with the Python backend included. No separate Python installation is needed.
- Check signed application updates on the Stable or Alpha channel. Review the version and release notes before applying an update. Desktop updates finish after the app closes and retain a backup for interrupted-update recovery.
- Use the same versioned backend API from the desktop app, Decky, or CLI. Application replacement is blocked while firmware workers are active, including workers using a custom state directory.

**Firmware support remains limited.** macOS and Windows support device discovery, firmware identity queries, and firmware browsing/preparation. Firmware installation and recovery are disabled on those operating systems until their write paths are validated. Linux retains the specifically reviewed receiver update and recovery paths; this release does not enable firmware installation for every 8BitDo model or wireless controller updates.

**The macOS and Windows installers are not OS-signed.** They have no Apple Developer ID/notarization or Windows Authenticode signature, so the operating system may warn about or block launching them. TUF signatures verify application-update content; they do not replace OS publisher signing.

This is a prerelease. Select **Alpha** to receive subsequent alpha application updates. Updating the app does not update any controller firmware or authorize a firmware write.

This alpha fixes receiver update workers failing to start from Decky when its backend has no desktop-session environment.

- Protected workers now connect to the current user's verified session bus. Suspend protection remains required; an unavailable session produces a clear error before launching a firmware worker.
- Both frontends label unsupported models and manual downloads **Download firmware only**. Preparation explains when the selected firmware is already installed or a source-to-destination update is unsupported.
- Existing receiver installation authorizations are unchanged. Controller flashing over USB, 2.4 GHz, and Bluetooth remains unavailable. This release does not enable additional firmware writes.

To update Decky, install `8bitdo-deck.zip` using **Decky Settings → Developer → Install Plugin from ZIP File**. No terminal environment exports are needed. Enable Developer mode under General if the page is hidden. Installing a desktop or CLI update does not upgrade Decky.

Existing standalone CLI installations can run:

```sh
eightbitdo app-update-check --channel alpha
eightbitdo app-update-apply 0.3.0a2 --channel alpha --confirm
```

Desktop installations can select **Alpha** in App settings, check for updates, and confirm the new version. macOS and Windows firmware writes remain disabled pending hardware validation; their installers still lack OS publisher signatures.

This alpha adds an experimental 2.4 GHz firmware update route for the Ultimate 2 Wireless controller on Linux, shared by Decky, the desktop app, and the CLI.

- Supported upgrade: stable controller **1.09 → exact official 1.10**, edition 1, through a USB-connected receiver running stable **1.06**. Both components' bootloader and application fingerprints must match the reviewed code. The controller must report at least 30% battery.
- Controller and receiver firmware remain separate. A controller already running 1.10 reports that no update is needed; the app does not downgrade or reinstall it automatically. Receiver 1.01 needs its separate USB update before it can carry wireless controller updates.
- Transfer verifies checksums, full readback, and erased sector padding before commit. The worker holds the receiver lock and sleep inhibitor through reconnection and checks the returning controller version.
- Interrupted wireless jobs retain their cached image and offer a separately confirmed USB recovery check and action. Recovery verifies the controller bootloader and firmware state before resetting a verified image or erasing and reinstalling the cached controller firmware. The USB recovery connection can use a different port from the receiver.
- Bluetooth updates, normal direct-USB controller installation, and macOS/Windows firmware writes remain unavailable. Existing receiver update authorizations are unchanged.

The USB controller boot-entry, inspection, and unchanged-firmware return passed on hardware. The full wireless transfer, USB rescue reinstall, and power-loss behavior have not been hardware-validated. This is source-reviewed experimental support, not a guarantee against bricking. See the [wireless evidence](https://github.com/trevor-scheer/8bitdo-deck/blob/v0.3.0-alpha.3/docs/devices/ultimate2-wireless.md) and [USB recovery contract](https://github.com/trevor-scheer/8bitdo-deck/blob/v0.3.0-alpha.3/docs/devices/ultimate2-controller-recovery.md) for the tested scope.

Install `8bitdo-deck.zip` with Decky's ZIP installer. Standalone apps can check the **Alpha** update channel; updating a standalone app does not replace the Decky plugin.

# 0.3.0-alpha.4

Decky now checks identified devices and prepares their newest stable firmware automatically. Select **Install** beside a ready device, or **Update all** at the top. The click starts installation without a separate review screen.

- Compact device rows show model artwork, installed and available versions, and status. Firmware details, manual downloads, USB setup, and diagnostics are available under **Details** or **More options**.
- Update all runs a persistent queue, one device at a time. Closing the sidebar does not stop it. A failed or unverified update stops the queue and retains the affected device's recovery controls.
- A completed queue checks devices again. If a receiver update makes its controller eligible, installing that newly available update takes another click.
- Latest-version selection compares firmware versions rather than relying on catalog order. Up-to-date devices skip downloads. Unsupported latest firmware remains unavailable; the plugin does not silently substitute an older image.

Automatic preparation does not write firmware. Device identity, source/destination authorization, image validation, USB access, battery checks, and suspend protection still apply. Experimental routes retain their existing validation limits; this release does not qualify additional devices or firmware versions. The desktop and CLI installation flows are unchanged.

Install the release's `8bitdo-deck.zip` through Decky to upgrade. See the [Decky setup guide](../decky-requirements.md).
